articles.title: 高雄 OTC 幣商「金牛百匯」涉詐團洗錢 6.86 億，母子主嫌等 26 人起訴
articles.excerpt:
高雄地檢署偵結起訴自稱「南部最大 OTC」的地下幣商「金牛百匯」，60 歲汪黃姓負責人與擔任執行長的兒子等 2 […]

〈 高雄 OTC 幣商「金牛百匯」涉詐團洗錢 6.86 億，母子主嫌等 26 人起訴 〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《 動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體 》。

高雄地檢署偵結起訴自稱「南部最大 OTC」的地下幣商「金牛百匯」，60 歲汪黃姓負責人與擔任執行長的兒子等 26 人，涉嫌替詐騙集團洗錢。檢方統計全台有 395 名被害人，洗錢金額 6 億 8,600 萬餘元。 （前情提要：行銷公司員工猝死牽出 201 億 USDT 洗錢平台，台灣只是分據點） （背景補充：金管會：台灣加密專法預計明年Q1上路，現有交易所 21 個月內要拿牌照） 重點摘要 高雄幣商金牛百匯涉替詐團洗錢 6.86 億元，26 人遭起訴 檢方統計 395 人受害，估算應沒收違法利得 2.32 億元 起訴書指業者賣幣比市價高 6% 到 10%，並提供教戰手冊 自稱「南部最大 OTC」的高雄地下幣商「金牛百匯」，涉嫌替詐騙集團洗錢。高雄地檢署偵結後，起訴負責人母子等 26 人。全案有 395 名被害人。檢方統計經手洗錢金額 6 億 8,600 萬餘元，等於平均每名被害人對應約 174 萬元。 檢方指出，金牛百匯由 60 歲汪黃姓女子擔任負責人，31 歲的汪姓兒子擔任執行長。公司 2021 年起以「南部最大 OTC」對外招攬客戶。檢方指控，業者以買賣虛擬資產為名，招攬詐團與車手上門洗錢。OTC 指不透過集中化交易所，由買賣雙方直接成交。 被起訴的包括母子兩人、核心管理階層與各分店櫃台員工。罪嫌有違反組織犯罪防制條例、三人以上共同詐欺取財、洗錢防制法與商業會計法。檢方也建請法院對主導犯罪的核心成員從重量刑。 賣幣價格比市價高 6% 到 10% 據聯合報引述起訴書，金牛百匯把虛擬資產售價訂得比市價高 6% 到 10%。等於每買 100 萬元的幣，要多付 6 萬到 10 萬元。起訴書指出，業者藉此過濾客戶並朋分暴利。 業者也承諾協助客戶申辦境外交易所帳號，再把虛擬資產轉入詐團錢包。業者還提供教戰手冊，指導被害人應付詢問。檢方認為，業者利用境外交易所製造金流斷點，讓資金去向更難追查。 聯合報報導，「金牛百匯國際開發有限公司」沒有依法向金管會完成洗錢防制法遵聲明。執行長掌管冷錢包與交易所帳號，公司在全台設有多家分店，聘用員工擔任櫃台、會計與行銷。業者還投放廣告、滿額贈禮、代客叫車，把自己包裝成合法金融機構。 內部群組被指嘲諷被害人 金牛百匯內部 LINE 群組不時有人嘲諷被害人。群組裡出現「明顯就是被騙了」、「那麼蠢活該要被騙」等留言。檢警調查認為，公司從上到下都知道客戶遭詐，仍配合洗錢。 聯合報報導，檢方調查發現業者明知沒有合法幣商資格，仍頻繁接觸詐騙集團。這些集團有的自稱「做詐的」、「資金盤」，有的以假交友、假投資行騙。業者沒有拒絕，還設計出一套「一條龍」商業模式，也涉嫌配合車手頭規避大額通貨交易申報。 金牛百匯也涉嫌從 2023 年 10 月起不依法開立發票，以掩蓋持續違法營業。業者開立的會計憑證被指只選擇性填寫極低金額，藉此逃漏稅捐。 常見問題 金牛百匯洗錢案有多少人被起訴 高雄地檢署起訴 26 人，包括 60 歲汪黃姓負責人、31 歲擔任執行長的兒子，以及幹部與各分店櫃台員工，罪名涉及組織犯罪、加重詐欺與洗錢。 金牛百匯洗錢金額是 6.86 億還是 30 億 6 億 8,600 萬餘元是檢方統計 395 名被害人對應的洗錢金額，近 30 億元是聯合報報導的經手金流，兩個數字的計算範圍不同。 相關報導 幣想交易所為詐團洗錢！主謀施啟仁一審重判 22 年，金流超過 23 億元 Youtube頻道「交易幣修課」導師涉當詐騙首腦，誘會員到假平台買USDT 台中女信貸、押房買金條換 USDT，出金才知被騙 1500 萬〈高雄 OTC 幣商「金牛百匯」涉詐團洗錢 6.86 億，母子主嫌等 26 人起訴〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。

articles.excerpt:
據 公開資訊觀測站重大訊息，三商投資控股（2905）11 月 13 日盤後公布第三季財報，單季每股虧損 39. […]

〈 台股》三商單季每股虧 39 元，是股價 2.4 倍！主因是和玉山金換股 〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《 動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體 》。

據 公開資訊觀測站重大訊息，三商投資控股（2905）11 月 13 日盤後公布第三季財報，單季每股虧損 39.35 元，約是當天收盤價的 2.4 倍。主因是持有的三商美邦人壽股票 9 月 1 日換成玉山金控股票，認列處分投資損失約 421.2 億元，換股過程沒有付出現金。 （前情提要：黃仁勳辭職隔天，台股不跌反漲 1,300 點，聯發科、世芯、創意(ASIC三雄)開盤漲停） （背景補充：比特幣能當銀行擔保品？玉山銀行、PwC 齊聚台灣區塊鏈年會，探討授信新課題） 重點摘要 三商第三季單季每股虧 39.35 元，約是股價 2.4 倍 三商美邦人壽換股玉山金，認列處分損失 421.2 億元 11/13 收盤計，三商持有玉山金市值是自身 1.5 倍 三商投資控股（2905）11 月 13 日盤後在公開資訊觀測站公布第三季財報。第三季單季歸屬母公司淨損 414.6 億元，每股虧損 39.35 元。三商當天收盤價 16.15 元，單季每股虧損約是股價的 2.4 倍。財報在收盤後才公布，當天的股價還沒有反映這份財報。 虧損主要來自「換股」，三商與子公司原本持有三商美邦人壽普通股 2,141,527,710 股。9 月 1 日股份轉換基準日，每 1 股三商美邦人壽換發 0.2596 股玉山金控。三商因此取得玉山金普通股 555,940,590 股。三商同日另發重大訊息，說明這次換股認列處分投資損失約 421.2 億元，計入當期損益。 依第三季合併綜合損益表，三商第三季單季稅前淨損 428.2 億元，其中 421.2 億元就是這筆處分損失。三商第二季單季每股還賺 1.90 元，上半年累計每股盈餘 1.93 元。換股損失認列後，前三季累計歸屬母公司淨損 394.2 億元，每股虧損 37.41 元。 421 億元是帳面差額，換股沒有付現 依三商公告，這筆損失是兩個數字的差額。一邊是換入的玉山金股票公允價值，另一邊是帳上原本的三商美邦人壽投資帳面價值，包含相關權益項目。三商帳上記錄的三商美邦人壽價值，比換到手的玉山金股票高出約 421 億元。換股完成後，這個落差要一次反映在損益表上。 整個過程是股票換股票，三商沒有付出現金。9 月底三商歸屬母公司業主的權益仍有 266.3 億元，公司公告的每股淨值為 25.28 元。處分損失 421.2 億元，約是三商 11 月 13 日收盤市值的 2.3 倍。 三商美邦人壽今年 1 月 1 日起適用保險合約會計準則 IFRS 17。追溯重編的影響直接調整資本公積、保留盈餘等權益項目，不經過損益表。 三商公告列出五項對保留盈餘的影響。IFRS 17 追溯重編讓保留盈餘增加 318.1 億元，重新指定金融資產增加 32.7 億元。1 到 8 月認列的保留盈餘與其他權益轉列，分別增加 22.3 億元與 66.3 億元。唯一減少的是 421.2 億元處分損失。 五項相抵後，保留盈餘淨增加 18.3 億元，等於處分損失在保留盈餘這一欄已被另外四項抵掉。三商註明，這個金額只涵蓋這五項調節，完整變動要看第三季合併財報。 換來的玉山金，市值比三商自己高五成 以 11 月 13 日證交所收盤價計算，玉山金收 48.3 元。三商與子公司持有的 555,940,590 股，市值約 268.5 億元。三商已發行普通股 1,110,371,703 股，收盤價 16.15 元，市值約 179.3 億元。三商集團手上的玉山金股票，市值約是三商本身的 1.5 倍。 這批持股約占玉山金已發行股數的 3.1%。換股後改列為按公允價值衡量的金融資產，帳面價值會跟著玉山金股價變動。三商 9 月底合併總資產 599.8 億元，總負債 257.7 億元。9 月 1 日之後，三商沒有在公開資訊觀測站發布處分玉山金股票的重大訊息。 換股比例 8 月調高，9 月 1 日完成轉換 三商在 2025 年 11 月 5 日首次公告這項換股案。三商以股份轉換方式，處分所持三商美邦人壽全部股份，換取玉山金新發行的普通股。2026 年 8 月 14 日，三商公告調高換股比例。每股三商美邦人壽可換的玉山金，從 0.2486 股調高為 0.2596 股，股份轉換基準日訂在 9 月 1 日。 依 8 月 14 日公告，母公司三商直接持有 1,836,519,880 股並全數參與轉換。這部分預計換得玉山金 476,760,560 股。其餘的玉山金股票來自子公司。三商行換得 32,458,450 股，三商食品換得 36,020,409 股。三商餐飲、三商電腦等子公司持有的少量三商美邦人壽股票，也一併轉換。 常見問題 三商第三季為什麼每股虧 39 元 三商持有的三商美邦人壽股票 9 月 1 日換成玉山金，換入股票的公允價值低於原帳面價值，認列處分損失約 421.2 億元。 三商換股玉山金的 421 億損失是現金虧損嗎 不是現金支出。這筆損失是帳面價值與玉山金股票公允價值的差額，換股沒有付現。三商 9 月底每股淨值仍有 25.28 元。 相關報導 台灣4家金控傳有意併購VASP交易所，MaiCoin、幣託都在名單；富邦、聯邦銀行先卡位 〈 麻吉大哥在 Papertrade 爆倉 2,100 次虧 222 萬鎂！丟無聊猿讓網友抽 〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《 動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體 》。

「麻吉大哥」Machibigbrother 在永續合約平台 Papertrade 已被清算超過 2,100 次，累計虧損 222 萬美元。扣掉平台獎勵，他仍虧約 171 萬美元。他 11 月 9 日把 Hyperliquid 的資金轉往 Papertrade，同一週還把無聊猿與變異猿放進自己的扭蛋池讓網友抽。 （前情提要：麻吉大哥 Hyperliquid 只剩1美元！一個月虧掉千萬還被幣安害到） （背景補充：贏了要排隊，輸了能領幣：一次看懂 Papertrade「爆倉即挖礦」的 1000 倍莊家生意） 重點摘要 黃立成在 Papertrade 被清算逾 2,100 次，虧損 222 萬美元 扣掉 51.4 萬美元獎勵，他在 Papertrade 仍虧約 171 萬美元 Ember 統計他在 Hyperliquid 一年半虧損 3,746 萬美元 鏈上數據分析帳號 Lookonchain 11 月 13 日發文，「麻吉大哥」在 Papertrade 已被清算超過 2,100 次。他在這個永續合約平台累計虧損 222 萬美元，約新台幣 7,300 萬元（依 14 日匯率換算）。這則貼文在台灣時間 13 日下午 4 點 32 分發出，至 14 日上午約有 7.2 萬次觀看。 同一週， Machi 在 X 上連發推文，把無聊猿（BAYC）與變異猿（MAYC）放進自己的扭蛋池「MachiPool」。網友用 MachiPool 代幣抽獎。他在推文中寫的每抽價格，介於 3 到 8 美元。 扣掉獎勵仍虧 171 萬美元 Lookonchain 附上的帳戶截圖顯示，這個地址的歷史損益是負 222 萬美元。他已領取約 51.4 萬美元的平台獎勵，扣掉後仍虧約 171 萬美元。帳戶累計交易量 19.3 億美元，約是虧損金額的 870 倍。 截圖當下，帳戶淨值只剩約 407 美元，未平倉部位的名目價值約 18.6 萬美元。 截圖這一頁的清算紀錄都是 ETH 多單，單筆虧損從 73.89 到 2,063.01 美元不等。以總虧損除以 2,100 次粗算，平均每次約 1,057 美元。這是動區自行換算，總虧損也含沒有爆倉的虧損單。 從 Hyperliquid 轉到 Papertrade Machi 先前主要在 Hyperliquid 上做多 ETH。Lookonchain 9 日指出，他在市場下跌中再度被完全清算。他把 Hyperliquid 剩下的 1.661 萬美元，轉到 Papertrade 繼續交易。 當時他在 Papertrade 已虧 162 萬美元，扣掉 48.5 萬美元獎勵仍虧 114 萬美元。到 13 日，他在 Papertrade 的虧損又多了約 60 萬美元。 Papertrade 架在 Hyperliquid 上，10 月 10 日上線，官網標榜「合成永續合約」與最高 1,000 倍槓桿。平台由協議擔任所有部位的對手方。平台代幣 PAPER 在用戶實現虧損或被清算時鑄造，虧得越多領得越多。 常見問題 麻吉大哥黃立成在 Papertrade 虧了多少錢 據 Lookonchain 11 月 13 日統計，黃立成在 Papertrade 被清算超過 2,100 次，累計虧損 222 萬美元。扣掉已領的 51.4 萬美元獎勵，他仍虧約 171 萬美元。 Papertrade 是什麼平台 Papertrade 是架在 Hyperliquid 上的合成永續合約平台，10 月 10 日上線，最高 1,000 倍槓桿。用戶虧損或被清算時，平台會鑄造代幣 PAPER 作為獎勵。 相關報導 Papertrade 日入僅次 Tether：把九成抽水退給輸家的賭場 麻吉大哥缺這點錢？1 ETH 拋售變異猿，帳面虧損約 85% 麻吉大哥最新訪談》死扛 3,000 萬鎂虧損不賣！重倉三百隻 BAYC、揭密 Web3 狂人投資學〈麻吉大哥在 Papertrade 爆倉 2,100 次虧 222 萬鎂！丟無聊猿讓網友抽〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。

索尼宣布《战神：斯巴达之子》推出 PS4 版，新增两种游戏模式
articles.excerpt:
IT之家 11 月 14 日消息，索尼圣莫尼卡工作室宣布 2D 动作平台游戏《战神：斯巴达之子》将于 11 月 16 日登陆 PS4，发售时间为当地时间午夜。

 

《战神：斯巴达之子》此前已于 2026 年 2 月 12 日率先登陆 PS5，由 Mega Cat Studios 与 Santa Monica Studio 合作开发，是一款采用复古像素美术风格的 2D 动作平台游戏。故事以年轻时期的奎托斯为主角，讲述他与弟弟戴莫斯在斯巴达接受严酷训练期间的经历。

 

价格方面，游戏标准版售价为 29.99 美元 / 29.99 欧元 / 24.99 英镑 / 3,480 日元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 145.5 元人民币） ，数字豪华版 39.99 美元 / 39.99 欧元 / 32.99 英镑 / 4,480 日元 （现汇率约合 187.3 元人民币） 。

 

除 PS4 版本外，开发团队还将于 11 月 16 日推出免费更新，为 PS4 和 PS5 版本加入两种新游戏模式。

 

其中，Hermes Mode（赫尔墨斯模式）主要面向速通玩家，提供分段计时器、持久化成绩排行榜等速通工具。玩家首次通关后即可解锁该模式，也可以在游戏开始菜单输入以下按键组合提前开启：上、上、下、下、左、右、左、右、L1、R1、触摸板。

 

另一种模式为 Erebus Mode（厄瑞玻斯模式），采用一击必杀机制，玩家和敌人均只需受到一次攻击便会倒下，为游戏带来更高的挑战难度。

 

两种模式均需要在开始新游戏并选择存档槽时确定。官方特别提醒，一旦为某个存档选择游戏模式，后续便无法更改该存档对应的模式。

articles.title: Over $600m was raised across 14 deals this week
articles.excerpt:
It was another slow week for FinTech deals as the end of 2026 edges closer.  A total of $602m was raised across 14 FinTech deals this week, a small increase on the previous week where $454.4m was raised across 12 deals. There were three deals that exceeded $100m this week. The biggest deal of the […]

The post Over $600m was raised across 14 deals this week appeared first on FinTech Global .

It was another slow week for FinTech deals as the end of 2026 edges closer.  

A total of $602m was raised across 14 FinTech deals this week, a small increase on the previous week where $454.4m was raised across 12 deals.

There were three deals that exceeded $100m this week. The biggest deal of the week was raised by PayTech company Imprint, which raised $130m in a funding round led by existing investor Khosla Ventures.

The funding round valued the PayTech company at $1.9bn. This was not the only FinTech unicorn of the week. Databento was another unicorn that secured funds this week, securing $100m in its Series C round.

The only other deal to exceed $100m this week was Brazil-based Clara, which closed a funding round on $105m. The deal was comprised of a $65m Series C and a renewed $40m facility from General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund (CVF).

In terms of location, the US was home to the most deals with six. It was home to Imprint, Databento, Bay, geniosAI, Marble and Agentcard.

The only other country to record multiple deals this week was Isreal with two deals (Dreeze and Brava).

The other countries to secure funds this week were UK (Griffin), Denmark (Sumary), Germany (Pliant), Brazil (Clara), Switzerland (Light Frame) and Australia (Nagaris).

Recent research from FinTech Global this week found that US FinTech funding hit a five-quarter high with a 69% growth in Q3. US FinTech market attracted $19.3bn across 472 deals in Q3 2026, the highest level of both funding and deal activity across the five-quarter period.

 

In terms of sectors it was balanced between for four. These sub-sectors were infrastructure and enterprise software (Clara, Sumary and Nagaris), CyberTech (Bay, Brava and Dreeze), WealthTech (Griffin, Marble and Light Frame) and PayTech (Imprint, Pliant and Agentcard).

The only other sub sector to record deals this week was data and analytics with two deals (geniosAI and Databento)

Here are the 14 deals covered on FinTech Global this week:

Imprint raises $130m as AI reshapes brand loyalty

 Imprint , the New York-based payments, loyalty and customer intelligence platform, has secured $130m in fresh financing that places its valuation at roughly $1.9bn. 

Khosla Ventures, already a backer of the company, led the round. Existing investors Hedosophia, Ribbit Capital, Spice and Thrive Capital also took part, alongside newcomer Positive Sum.

Imprint plans to use the capital to move into new payment options and build out AI capabilities, helping brands identify and reward their customers regardless of where or how they decide to pay.

The company now counts more than two million members and works with brands that together account for over $500bn of yearly US consumer spending. So far this year it has rolled out programmes with Albertsons Companies, Fanatics, Kroger and Shell, the last of which to go live being the Fanatics programme this week. Total cardholder spend across its partners more than doubled from 2025 to 2026, while the proportion of spending made with Imprint cards at partner checkouts grew threefold over the last 12 months. Imprint has also secured an extra $1.5bn in warehouse capacity and priced its second AAA-rated asset-backed securitisation, which drew investor demand close to five times the size of the offering.

Part of the new funding will go towards widening access to its products among partners’ customers.

Clara secures $105m to scale AI spend management in LatAm

 Clara , a corporate spend management platform operating across Latin America, has raised $105m through a mix of equity and growth capital, made up of a $65m Series C and a renewed $40m facility from General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund (CVF). 

Citius, Kaszek and DEG, which is part of Germany’s KfW Group, anchored the Series C. A number of existing backers also returned, including Acrew Capital, Citi Ventures, Coatue, Commerce Ventures, DST Global Partners, Gaingels, General Catalyst, Mana Ventures, Monashees and Notable Capital. Joining them as new investors were CMT Digital, a blockchain and digital asset investment specialist, Nascent VC, the team behind Mexico Tech Week, and Michael Gilroy.

The company has also passed the $100m mark in annualised net revenue and has recorded positive EBITDA for over a year.

The fresh funds will be used to grow Clara’s go-to-market team and to build out the automation and AI features of its platform. Through Model Context Protocol (MCP), the platform already links to major AI tools, letting customers pull live spend reports and forecasts by asking questions in plain language, while AI agents can carry out approved transactions on their own.

Its AI policy enforcement tool reviews staff expenses against company rules as they happen and passes any exceptions to human reviewers, cutting down on repetitive manual tasks. Clara Global allows businesses to oversee spending across multiple countries and currencies, including through stablecoins and multicurrency cards. Meanwhile, Clara Fleet and Clara Veículos provide fuel payment and management tools linked to the wider platform, offering an SAT-authorised fuel card with automatic tax invoicing in Mexico and a postpaid, open-loop corporate fuel card in Brazil.

Founded in 2021, Clara combines corporate cards, bill payments, spend management, accounts payable and accounts receivable within one AI-driven platform. By tying financial data to payment execution, it aims to help companies automate everyday tasks, keep spending under control and make sharper financial choices.

Databento hits $1.1bn valuation with $100m Series C

 Databento , a platform supplying market data to the modern financial industry, has secured $100m in a Series C round that values the business at $1.1bn. 

Fifth Down Capital, which backed Databento in its early days, led the investment. Almost every one of the firm’s existing backers returned to take part, among them NEA, DRW Venture Capital, Tribe Capital and Hedosophia.

Fitch Ventures also came on board as a strategic investor, adding the viewpoint of a major financial information business with significant experience in credit ratings, financial data and market analysis.

The raise comes only months after Databento closed a $97m Series B earlier in the year. In the period since that deal, the company has grown its revenue more than twofold and has stayed profitable throughout.

Databento’s client base spans top quantitative trading houses, brokerages, asset managers, commodities businesses and digital asset firms. It has also built a notable foothold in the artificial intelligence space, securing enterprise agreements with five of the six biggest frontier AI labs.

At the time the Series C closed, the company employed 39 people, meaning it crossed the $1.1bn valuation mark with a much smaller workforce than conventional market data vendors typically need.

Databento will put the fresh capital towards further development of its market data infrastructure and towards broadening its coverage into more asset classes.

The firm delivers both live and historical data covering futures, options, equities and indices, all accessible via a single API. Because it controls every layer of its technology, from the original data source through to final delivery, Databento says it is the first offering of its type to pair the speed and dependability required by the world’s top trading firms with a far easier experience for developers.

Pliant raises $80m as AI agents reshape B2B payments

 Pliant, a FinTech firm offering modular B2B payment services, has secured $80m in Series C funding to open more of its payment infrastructure to AI agents. 

The company says businesses are increasingly connecting AI agents directly to their financial systems.

Seaya Nova and Speedinvest co-led the round. Illuminate Financial, Motive Partners and Molten Ventures also invested. Pliant will use the capital to grow its presence in the United States and Canada, prepare launches in additional international markets and speed up its AI roadmap.

The raise comes after Pliant doubled its business in each of the last three years. It also follows soon after the company passed $100m in annual recurring revenue. Pliant has a workforce of over 300 people in eight offices and processes several billion dollars in payments each year for clients and partners in Europe and North America.

Pliant designed its platform on the assumption that AI will increasingly handle business payments. Its in-house AI agents take on repetitive finance tasks for customers at scale. External agents can connect to the platform through Model Context Protocol (MCP), including general assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT as well as automations that companies build themselves.

Bay raises $50m as AI agents test enterprise security limits

 Bay has come out of stealth with $50m in total funding and a customer roster that already includes Micron, Peloton, ClickUp and Wix, less than 12 months after it was founded. 

The capital comprises a $37m Series A led by Battery Ventures, alongside a $13m seed round that had not been made public until now, led by YL Ventures and Striker Venture Partners. Micron Ventures, Microsoft’s venture fund M12 and Wiz CEO Assaf Rappaport also backed the Series A.

The company’s origins trace back to an incident its founders experienced first-hand. One of their own coding agents attempted to open a cloud environment to the internet in order to finish a test. No attacker was involved.

The agent was simply using permissions it legitimately held to chase a valid objective, but in a hazardous manner.

Bay targets one of the main obstacles slowing AI uptake in large organisations: letting agents carry out critical tasks on their own while firms keep oversight and accountability. Its platform applies AI governance and enforcement across staff devices, cloud environments and SaaS tools, and can be deployed in under five minutes without requiring a persistent endpoint agent, kernel driver or network proxy.

Dreeze raises $33m as cloud recovery moves beyond data

 Dreeze , an Israeli and US cloud resilience company, has launched publicly with $33m in seed capital and made its Application Revival platform generally available. 

The platform is designed to restore complete cloud applications after an outage, rather than only their underlying data.

Norwest and Bessemer Venture Partners co-led the round, with Claltech also investing. The company will put the capital towards faster product development, larger sales and marketing teams, and wider enterprise adoption of Application Revival as organisations look for more dependable ways to restore cloud workloads.

The platform rests on four functions. The first, Know, uses autonomous dependency mapping to link each resource to the application it supports and to produce a recovery plan that updates as the live environment changes. The second, Protect, backs up data, configuration, keys and all other dependencies in an immutable, air-gapped vault, with optional replication across regions.

The third, Orchestrate, carries out the full recovery plan and rebuilds data, infrastructure, configuration, identity and connections in the order their dependencies require. The fourth, Validate, runs the entire plan as an automated end-to-end test that produces a working application, without affecting production systems or requiring manual cleanup.

Sumary raises $25m to challenge Europe’s accounting sector

 Sumary , a Copenhagen-founded AI operating system for accounting practices, has raised $25m in seed funding to accelerate its expansion across the UK and Europe, in what the company describes as the largest seed round for accounting software in Europe. 

The investment was led by Singular, with existing investors byFounders, Partech and Tenity also participating. The round attracted several angel investors, including Qonto co-founder Steve Anavi, Linear co-founder Tuomas Artman, Dust co-founder Stanislas Polu, Synthesia co-founder Steffen Tjerrild, Public.com co-founder Jannick Malling and Omnea co-founder Ben Freeman.

The latest funding comes less than a year after Sumary secured $4.2m in pre-seed investment, which ranked among Denmark’s largest pre-seed rounds. Since then, the company has secured contracts with several major accounting practices, including Deloitte, Grant Thornton and Baker Tilly, and signed up most of the 20 largest accounting firms in the Nordic region.

Sumary will use the capital to expand its presence across Europe, with London becoming its commercial headquarters while Denmark remains the centre for its technology development and AI research. Co-founders Pascar Sivam and Frederik Skov Wacher are relocating to London to lead the company’s UK growth. The business is also entering continental Europe, with the Benelux region selected as its first market.

The platform automates core accounting workflows, including monthly financial closes, VAT returns and year-end preparation. It operates across clients and their existing accounting ledgers, with completed work sent to accountants for review and approval. According to the company, accounting firms using the platform have reduced the time spent on monthly closes by 50% and VAT returns by 75% after three months.

Griffin raises $20m to add cards and stablecoin services

 Griffin , a UK-licensed bank serving FinTech firms and platforms, has closed a $20m Series B round that pushes its valuation beyond $100m and will fund a move into card issuing and stablecoin services. 

Octagon Partners led the investment, joined by existing backers including Notion Capital, A+ Ventures, Nordic Ninja and Breega.

Griffin plans to use the money to reach profitability and to drive its next growth stage, extending its agentic banking platform and giving businesses that build financial products access to a wider set of infrastructure.

The card issuing product will let Griffin’s customers roll out their own branded debit cards for both consumers and corporate users, combining cards with the accounts and payments that already sit on Griffin’s infrastructure. A credit card product is planned to follow soon after. On the stablecoin side, Griffin will build reserve capabilities for businesses active in the stablecoin market and add on-chain cross-border payments.

Griffin said the additions will turn its offering from core accounts, payments and compliance tooling into a far wider embedded finance stack. The company expects this to strengthen ties with current clients, open up more use cases and support its push towards sustainable profitability.

geniosAI lands $19.1m to make financial analysis traceable

 geniosAI , a financial intelligence platform aimed at changing how institutions carry out analysis and retain their know-how, has secured $19.1m across combined seed and Series A funding. 

FactSet led the Series A, with Zoom and General Catalyst also backing the company. geniosAI is developing products for the office of the CFO, as well as for investment professionals working on both the buy side and the sell side.

Through the partnership, FactSet’s data will be combined with geniosAI’s proprietary platform, giving finance and investment teams analysis they can trace, review, verify and develop further. Zoom supports the conversations in which decisions are taken, from internal finance reviews to earnings calls, and geniosAI aims to bring financial intelligence directly into those discussions.

The platform is already being used by finance and investment teams at leading Fortune 500 global banks and technology firms to prepare for earnings. This includes benchmarking results against peers and analyst forecasts, identifying notable findings and anticipating the questions analysts are likely to raise.

Brava raises $15m to prove SOC detections actually work

 Brava has emerged from stealth with $15m in seed funding, as enterprises hand more security decisions to AI agents that rely on unproven detection logic. 

The round was led by F2 Venture Capital and Pitango. Angel investors also took part, among them executives from Anthropic, Microsoft and Check Point. Brava says it already counts Fortune 100 firms in retail, energy and hospitality among its clients.

Brava’s multi-agent system recreates the evidence a genuine attack would leave behind. It models attacker behaviour and produces the precise telemetry an attack would generate in a customer’s environment, without running the attack itself. The platform handles more than 2.4 trillion events daily across client environments, with thousands of detections validated each day.

That ground truth supports three functions that sit alongside a customer’s existing SIEM. For detection engineering, Brava checks each rule against its intended attack, flags those that fail to trigger, rewrites them in the SIEM’s native query language using only fields confirmed present, and verifies they now fire. Broken rules, schema drift and inactive log sources are flagged on the day they occur.

For investigation, its agent Aquarium accepts plain English questions, plans the queries, searches the SIEM, archived logs, EDR and cloud audit trails together, and produces a report linking each finding to the underlying raw events. For data pipelines, Brava routes only the events detections need to the SIEM and shifts the remainder to cheaper, still searchable storage, a change the company says has lowered SIEM costs by 65% to 85% across its customers.

Marble raises $11m seed to finance AI compute

 Marble , a capital markets firm focused on frontier markets and AI infrastructure finance, has come out of stealth with $11m in seed funding to build out its institutional trading and private credit operations. 

Polychain Capital led the round. Maven 11, Ripple, Susquehanna Crypto, Lattice and Blockwall also took part, along with other venture and strategic backers and a small group of angel investors with an AI focus.

The company runs two divisions. Marble Compute is developing private credit infrastructure that links institutional lenders with neoclouds and GPU operators expanding AI capacity. Marble Markets is creating a platform where institutions can trade digital assets, real-world assets, prediction markets and compute, with Marble acting as counterparty.

Marble Compute is aimed at smaller, independent operators. The biggest listed neoclouds can raise money through public markets and major banks, but mid-market players often struggle to secure financing even when buyers have already committed to their capacity.

Agentcard secures $8m to let AI agents shop online

 Agentcard , a payments firm that lets AI agents make purchases using their users’ own cards, has closed an $8m seed funding round to help agents buy anything on the internet. 

Peak XV, Fin Capital and Y Combinator provided the capital. Several well-known technology figures have also backed the company. They include Y Combinator co-founder Paul Graham, OpenAI board member Adam D’Angelo, Shopify CEO Tobi Lütke and Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch. WorkOS CEO Michael Grinich, HubSpot CTO Dharmesh Shah, Rappi CEO Simón Borrero, and Darragh Buckley, founder and CEO of Increase, are also backers.

Agentcard’s platform is built for businesses developing AI agents. When they integrate the technology, each of their users only needs to register a card a single time. The card number is always hidden from the agent. Users approve each transaction with a passkey, Face ID or their voice, or they can set up automatic approvals.

Light Frame bags $5.1m to modernise private banking tech

 Light Frame , a provider of core banking and portfolio management software for wealth managers, has secured $5.1m in an oversubscribed Seed round as uptake of its platform grows among institutions across EMEA. 

Fortino Ventures led the investment, joined by new backers Sidekick Partners, Tenity, Chamaeleon and Altair Capital. Earlier supporters Rogue Venture Partners, New Stack Ventures and Studio Alpha also took part.

The raise comes as more institutions in the EMEA region take on Light Frame’s software. The business is already running live client operations and is building its footprint in private banking and wealth management.

Light Frame plans to put the new capital into further platform development, more capacity for implementation and client delivery, and growing its commercial operations, with an initial focus on EMEA.

The company argues that much of the wealth sector still depends on systems designed decades ago, leaving firms with infrastructure that takes too long to deploy, costs too much to run and struggles to keep up with changing demands.

In response, Light Frame has built core banking and portfolio management tools aimed squarely at wealth managers. Its platform brings banking and investment functions together on a cloud-native, API-first foundation built with AI at its centre.

Using built-in AI tools and a secure interoperability layer, clients can automate complicated processes, help staff work more efficiently and offer more advanced services to their customers. Because the system is fully modular, firms can either upgrade specific parts of their current setup or move to the full platform, cutting deployment time, complexity and overall cost of ownership.

Nagaris secures A$1.26m ($850k) seed for AI accounting platform

 Nagaris , a platform built to run Australian accounting practices, has completed a seed equity round worth A$1.26m, backed in part by the partners behind AI-native accounting firm BPAG Accountants. 

The partners of the five practices that combined to create BPAG took part in the round. They were joined by several other accounting firms, a group of private investors and the founder of Nagaris. Best Practice Group helped arrange the investment.

The round closed in August 2026 and was made up entirely of ordinary shares. Nagaris plans to put the capital towards developing its product further.

Within the platform, an assistant called Ask Nagaris draws on more than 80 specialist skills to produce first drafts of everyday tasks, including BAS workpapers, Division 7A calculations, research notes and letters to clients. Because the system creates workpapers directly from a client’s Xero data, a BAS that once demanded over 90 minutes of preparation can now be reviewed and approved in around 10 minutes, though more complicated returns take longer. Every output is checked and approved by a qualified accountant, and no material is sent to clients or the ATO without human sign-off. Over a fortnight, 54 BPAG staff used the assistant close to 2,000 times.

Nagaris also produces the Nagaris AI Accounting Index, which grades AI models against 112 questions on Australian accounting, and routes each query to whichever model configuration performs strongest. In addition to BPAG, a further 50 accounting firms are using the platform.

articles.title: Nakamoto Extends $60M Kraken Loan, Adds Bitcoin Derivatives to Its Collateral
articles.excerpt:
Nakamoto has bought itself more breathing room on its Kraken loan, as the remaining $165 million is now scheduled across 2027.

The Bitcoin-native holding company founded by David Bailey, Nakamoto, has bought itself another year before part of its Kraken debt comes due.

But it still owes $165 million in USDT, which, interestingly, is more than the market values the company.

Kraken Loan

The firm said its subsidiary, Nakamoto Holdings, amended its agreement with Kraken to move the maturity date on $60 million from December 4, 2026, to December 4, 2027. The remaining $105 million is due on June 30, 2027, meaning none of the loan principal is scheduled to mature this year. The change spreads repayments across two dates next year rather than leaving a payment due in December 2026.

Nakamoto will include the net value of its Bitcoin derivatives positions held in its pledged Kraken trading account as collateral, although the amendment sets limits.

Commenting on the development, Tyler Evans, Chief Investment Officer of Nakamoto, said ,

 
“This amendment extends our runway and makes our collateral position more resilient. It gives us more flexibility to manage through Bitcoin price volatility so we can put our full attention on what we control: building our operating businesses and managing our Bitcoin holdings so that we can continue to grow through this market cycle. We are grateful to Kraken for being a supportive financing partner.”

BTC Sales Helped Reduce Debt

Nakamoto initially took out $210 million in December 2025, before trimming its debt by $45 million in June. It raised roughly $48 million by selling Bitcoin and derivatives, using most of that cash to bring down what it owed.

By the end of September, the Bitcoin treasury firm had pledged 3,030 of its 4,283 BTC holdings to Kraken as collateral, according to its latest quarterly report. Those coins were worth around $253 million at the time, when the crypto asset was trading near $83,500. At the current price of $69,334, their value has fallen to roughly $210 million. That’s still about 127% of the $165 million Nakamoto owes Kraken.

articles.title: The Last Mile Remains a Pain Point for Cross-Border Payments
articles.excerpt:
It often takes a series of intermediaries to complete a single cross-border payment. While most stages of the process have become significantly faster, the final leg of the journey continues to drive delays and costs. Global messaging network Swift plays a central role in facilitating international transactions, and the organization recently studied payment processing times […]

The post The Last Mile Remains a Pain Point for Cross-Border Payments appeared first on PaymentsJournal .

It often takes a series of intermediaries to complete a single cross-border payment. While most stages of the process have become significantly faster, the final leg of the journey continues to drive delays and costs.

Global messaging network Swift plays a central role in facilitating international transactions, and the organization recently studied payment processing times across 40 markets. The research found that roughly half of all transactions on Swift’s network reach recipient institutions within 40 seconds.

This suggests that much of the remaining friction in cross-border payments occurs after a transaction reaches the receiving institution but before the funds are credited to the beneficiary’s account—a stage commonly known as the last mile.

Swift sees greater connectivity between international payment networks and domestic instant payment systems as one way to narrow this gap. Faster connections between the could reduce delays, improve payment transparency, and give financial institutions a more predictable experience to offer their customers.

Falling Short of the Roadmap

Swift’s findings underscore how some of the most persistent challenges in cross-border payments remain unsolved, despite years of work by the financial industry and regulators toward a Group of 20 (G20) roadmap designed to improve cross-border payments by next year.

While there has been some progress toward these objectives , including the implementation of the ISO 20022 messaging protocol and the stronger anti-money laundering standards, high fees, delays, and limited transparency continue to affect international transactions.

Spearheading Improvements

Even as these challenges persist, new initiatives aimed at improving international payments continue to emerge, many spearheaded by Swift. The organization recently developed a framework for retail cross-border payments , driven in part by growing consumer demand for cross-border payments and remittances in major markets.

Swift also highlighted the framework’s performance since its launch in June. Some transactions have already been completed in seconds, including a payment from Australia to India in 37 seconds and another from Brazil to the U.S. in one minute.

Beyond retail payments, Swift has been involved in several other initiatives, including testing tokenized deposits transfers across its network and developing a proof of concept for using alias identifiers in cross-border transactions. The concept would allow banks to use identifiers like phone numbers and email addresses to send international payments.

Despite this momentum, many of these initiatives remain in the early stages and are still some distance from mainstream adoption. For now, getting a cross-border payment across the finish line is likely an ongoing challenge for the industry.

articles.title: Circle Exec Frames USDC as Consumer Utility, Not Financial Tool
articles.excerpt:
Circle's chief product officer Nikhil Chandhok argues the winning stablecoin will be the one easiest for billions to use.

The post Circle Exec Frames USDC as Consumer Utility, Not Financial Tool appeared first on The Fintech Times .

Circle ‘s chief product and technology officer Nikhil Chandhok is making a deliberately unfashionable argument about stablecoins: that the technical architecture matters far less than whether an ordinary person with a phone can use USDC without knowing what a blockchain is. 

 Nikhil Chandhok, CPTO at Circle 

Speaking at TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco and in a subsequent interview with Fintech Nexus , Chandhok drew on two decades of consumer-product experience at Google, YouTube and Meta to argue that stablecoin adoption will be determined by design, not by protocol competition.

“Everyone thinks about stablecoins as a financial instrument,” he said. “I think about it as a consumer problem.”

 The consumer-product frame 

Chandhok’s career makes the framing credible. He launched the YouTube app on the first iPhone in 2007, helped build YouTube Music into the platform’s top revenue driver and led Meta ‘s augmented reality glasses programme before joining Circle. His read is that consumer technology succeeds when it delivers a concrete improvement in someone’s life without asking them to understand how it works.

Applied to USDC, the target use case is not sophisticated DeFi users but the Brazilian entrepreneur paying a Chinese supplier, the migrant worker sending a remittance, or the small business in a dollar-scarce market trying to hedge local currency risk. For those users, access to dollars via a smartphone is, as Chandhok put it, a ten- or hundred-times improvement over the status quo. The complexity of on-chain settlement is irrelevant if it is invisible.

He identified two design principles he said are frequently misapplied. The first is simplicity: do not explain how the product works; demonstrate the value it delivers. The second is network utility: treat a stablecoin network the way engineers treat a communications protocol, where every new participant makes the system more useful for all existing participants, rather than as a financial tool to be optimised in isolation.

“If you reason about the problem as a network utility instead of treating it as a financial tool, you build products differently,” Chandhok said, noting that getting this framing backwards has derailed many design teams.

 Regulatory and competitive context 

The argument arrives at a significant moment for stablecoin regulation. In the US, the GENIUS Act and related Senate proposals have moved stablecoin legislation closer to the floor than at any point since Facebook’s Libra project prompted a Congressional backlash in 2019. In the EU, MiCA is now in force, and e-money token issuers face reserve, redemption and marketing requirements that directly shape the consumer-product decisions Chandhok is describing. Circle received an EU e-money institution licence in 2024, positioning USDC ahead of competitors in compliant European distribution.

USDC is the second-largest stablecoin by market capitalisation, behind Tether ‘s USDT. Tether has historically dominated emerging-market remittance and informal dollar corridors precisely because of its early distribution. Chandhok’s consumer-product thesis is partly a claim that Circle can compete on user experience where it cannot yet compete on network scale, and that regulatory clarity in Western markets will eventually redraw the competitive map.

The near-term test is whether programmability, which Chandhok flagged as a further differentiator, translates into adoption in agentic AI workflows, where autonomous software agents need to settle transactions without human sign-off. Circle has positioned USDC as infrastructure for that use case, though the market for AI-to-AI payments remains nascent and largely unregulated.

The post Circle Exec Frames USDC as Consumer Utility, Not Financial Tool appeared first on The Fintech Times .

articles.title: ‘People are chucking stuff like gold and Bitcoin’ as rising inflation leads investors to seek yield
articles.excerpt:
A brief comeback has given way to renewed selling, with analysts warning the road back could get rockier.

Bitcoin’s escape from the trenches didn’t last long. The cryptocurrency fell more than 4% on Friday to $68,500, wiping out gains built over the past three months and casting doubt on whether its bear market was ever really over.

The asset also faces weaker investor appetite, according to crypto analytics provider CryptoQuant. The firm’s demand indicator recorded its weakest reading since December 2023, while Bitcoin exchange-traded funds became net sellers again.

The recent downturn has also extended to other parts of the crypto market. That includes Tether’s USDT, the largest cryptocurrency pegged to the U.S. dollar, whose total value shrank by $7.7 billion over the past two months, according to CryptoQuant, a sign that less cash is available in crypto markets.

This time around, inflation has been the main culprit. Tuesday’s Consumer Price Index report showed prices rose 0.4% in October, more than economists expected. Even stripping out food and energy, inflation ran hotter than forecast. Traders now overwhelmingly expect the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates by a quarter percentage point in December, with some betting on an even bigger increase.

“Because these are non-yielding assets, and we expect inflation to rise… people are chucking stuff like gold and Bitcoin to find… government bonds that are going up, providing you [with] income,” Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at financial technology company IG Group, told Fortune .

Bitcoin isn’t alone in its retreat. Gold traded near $3,900 an ounce on Friday, well below its January peak of about $5,600, according to financial data provider Trading Economics. Prices have fallen roughly 5% over the past month and nearly 5% from a year ago.

 Bitcoin’s bad year 

Friday’s drop dealt a fresh blow to Bitcoin investors, who had only recently found their footing after months of losses. After Bitcoin hit $58,000 in June, optimism returned in August when the U.S. Treasury announced plans to expand its bond buybacks . The announcement helped spark a rally that carried Bitcoin to $86,000 in September. Since then, though, it has been sliding again.

Recent political news has also made Bitcoin’s recovery an uphill battle, though it held its ground until Friday. The midterm elections handed Democrats control of Congress, a setback for a crypto industry that has leaned on Republican allies to advance favorable legislation. Still, Bitcoin initially took the results in stride.

That was largely because investors had seen the outcome coming , according to Stephen Coltman, head of macro at crypto asset manager 21Shares. “The midterm results weren’t a surprise, and they don’t change the regulatory interpretations as they stand today… We at least have some regulatory stability for two years,” he said.

Inflation and politics aren’t the only forces shaping Bitcoin’s outlook. Analysts say the cryptocurrency is also caught up in the AI boom, which is competing for investors’ money while helping keep the economy strong enough for interest rates to stay high. 

Heavy borrowing and spending on AI have created what 21Shares calls an “AI black hole,” drawing money toward the sector and away from assets like Bitcoin and gold. But Bitcoin remains “joined at the hip” with tech stocks, according to Beauchamp. That leaves it in an awkward position: It faces competition for investment dollars when enthusiasm for AI runs high, yet can get dragged down when that enthusiasm fades.

The boom also complicates the outlook for interest rates. In Coltman’s view, AI spending is helping prop up an otherwise weak economy, giving the Fed room to keep fighting inflation with higher rates. If rising borrowing costs force AI companies to rein in spending, the economy could weaken enough to push the Fed to change course, potentially giving Bitcoin some breathing room.

This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: ‘Draining the Economic Life and Soul’: Coffeezilla Turns Trump’s Own Words Against His Crypto Empire
articles.excerpt:
From World Liberty Financial to controversial meme coins, Coffeezilla follows the money behind the Trump family's rapidly expanding crypto empire.

Back in 2020, at a campaign rally in Ocala, Florida, Donald Trump said: “It’s a political class that enriched itself while draining the economic life and soul from our country.”

But Coffeezilla has discovered that many investments that made the Trump family billions of dollars may have actually caused most American investors to lose money. He said,

 
“It turns out Trump was right. There is a political class stealing from America, but it turns out all we’ve done is replaced one that was mediocre at it to one that’s incredibly good at it.”

Inside the Trump Family’s Crypto Empire

YouTuber and cryptocurrency investigator Coffeezilla, along with researcher Molly White, has published an extensive investigation into the US President’s family’s crypto businesses and has discovered that many investments that made them billions of dollars have actually caused most American investors to lose money.

The investigation mainly focuses on World Liberty Financial, the Trump family’s meme coins, foreign investments, as well as business relationships.

According to the investigation, World Liberty Financial was launched shortly before the 2024 presidential election, initially attracting limited interest from investors. However, after Trump won the election, its token sales reportedly reached $550 million.

One of the biggest investments came from an entity backed by UAE royal Sheik Tahnoun bin Zayed, which reportedly paid $500 million for a 49% stake in World Liberty just four days before Trump’s inauguration. The investigation questions why this investment was not disclosed when the platform later announced that its USD1 stablecoin would be used for MGX’s $2 billion investment in Binance. Sheik Tahnoun was behind both investments.

According to White, interest earned on USD1’s reserves could generate hundreds of millions of dollars for Trump family entities. Binance has also played a major role in the stablecoin’s growth through promotional campaigns and high-yield offers. The investigation also put the focus on how World Liberty could benefit from the GENIUS Act, stablecoin legislation promoted by Trump.

Another major concern involves the platform’s $1.5 billion deal with ALT5 Sigma, which reportedly generated around $500 million for a Trump family entity and $90 million for the Witkoff family. ALT5’s stock subsequently lost around 95% of its value over the following year. Possible conflicts of interest involving foreign investors and government officials, particularly given Steve Witkoff’s role as US Special Envoy to the Middle East, were also scrutinized.

Company Denies Any Wrongdoing

World Liberty Financial, for its part, has rejected the allegations, defending its business activities while maintaining that it has followed the required regulatory procedures. It also denied receiving special treatment or having any influence over government policies. The company maintains that its products and partnerships are legitimate business activities.

Given the controversy surrounding it, the launch of the TRUMP meme coin shortly before Trump returned to the White House in January 2025 was naturally a major part of the investigation. The token reportedly generated around $600 million, while Melania Trump’s token and NFT ventures brought in another $6 million. However, the TRUMP and MELANIA tokens later lost approximately 95% and 99% of their peak values, respectively, leaving many investors with heavy losses.

The investigation also covers Eric Trump and Donald Trump Jr.’s involvement in the Bitcoin mining company American Bitcoin and Trump Media’s crypto plans.

Perpetual futures have traditionally been associated with cryptocurrencies, and they’ve grown into a substantial market. According to CoinGecko Research figures cited by Forbes, crypto perpetuals average approximately $4.7 trillion in monthly trading volume. Now, the same trading model is expanding beyond digital assets, giving traders exposure to publicly listed companies and businesses preparing to go public.

 PrimeXBT is part of this shift. Having recently introduced Tokenized Stock Crypto Futures, the global multi-asset broker and crypto asset service provider is now preparing to expand its offering further with Pre-IPO Trading, starting with Anthropic*, the AI company behind Claude.

 

From crypto perpetuals to company-linked markets

The expansion of perpetual futures beyond cryptocurrencies gained momentum earlier this year, as major exchanges began introducing contracts linked to private companies such as SpaceX and OpenAI. Similar instruments linked to Anthropic subsequently appeared on other trading venues.

These contracts apply a familiar Crypto Futures structure to a different type of market. Rather than trading the underlying shares, traders take long or short positions through USDT-quoted derivatives. For listed companies, prices are influenced by movements in the underlying stock. For private companies preparing to go public, prices reflect market expectations about their potential valuations and upcoming listings.

SpaceX’s June IPO demonstrated the interest surrounding major public debuts. The company priced its shares at $135, opened at $150 and closed its first trading day at $160.95, approximately 19% above the IPO price. The listing also illustrated how expectations formed ahead of an IPO can differ from prices established once shares begin trading publicly.

PrimeXBT’s expansion with Tokenized Stocks

PrimeXBT began expanding into company-linked Crypto Futures in October, introducing seven Tokenized Stock Crypto Futures contracts linked to SpaceX, NVIDIA, Tesla, Circle, Apple, Alphabet and Robinhood. These USDT-quoted derivatives allow traders to take long or short positions on share price movements without owning the underlying shares.

Available 24/7, the contracts extend PrimeXBT’s Crypto Futures offering beyond cryptocurrencies, giving traders round-the-clock access to major companies through a crypto-native trading structure. PXTrader 2.0 supports accounts denominated in USD, USDT, USDC, BTC and ETH, allowing clients to access these markets through a single platform. TradingView-powered charts, price alerts, chart trading and mobile access provide tools for monitoring markets and managing positions. PrimeXBT also offers 24/7 live chat support.

 Milestones in company-linked perpetual contracts, from the first pre-IPO perpetuals to PrimeXBT’s Crypto Futures. Sources: exchange data, Forbes, PrimeXBT. 

Anthropic: The next step into pre-IPO markets

PrimeXBT is now preparing to introduce Pre-IPO Trading as a new category within its Crypto Futures offering, beginning with ANTHROPIC/USDT*. The USDT-margined perpetual will trade 24/7, allowing traders to take long or short positions on Anthropic’s market-implied valuation ahead of its public listing, without owning shares in the company.

Anthropic filed its public IPO registration with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on 26th October, proposing a Nasdaq listing under the ticker ANT. The company has since updated its filing with an indicative offering price of $70–$78 per share, with public trading expected to begin on 19th November.

Unlike Tokenized Stock Crypto Futures linked to publicly traded companies, ANTHROPIC/USDT will initially have no official share price to follow. Its price will instead be determined through a live order book, with one contract representing one notional share. This assumption is used for contract pricing and does not represent Anthropic’s official share count or valuation.

Following Anthropic’s public debut, the contract is designed to transition into a standard perpetual Crypto Futures contract linked to the listed stock. If the IPO is cancelled, the contract may be delisted, with open positions closed or settled at a reference price following advance notice. It will not convert into actual shares.

What’s next for Crypto Futures?

The expansion of Crypto Futures beyond cryptocurrencies is opening up new opportunities for traders to access major market developments, from the performance of established global companies to highly anticipated public listings.

With Tokenized Stock Crypto Futures already available and Pre-IPO Trading planned to launch, PrimeXBT is bringing these opportunities together on PXTrader 2.0. articles.title: OpenAI 推 ChatGPT Wallet：AI 代理替你付款，不碰卡號
articles.excerpt:
OpenAI 推出 ChatGPT Wallet，讓 AI 代理 dots 用單次交易代碼替用戶付款、拿不到真實卡號，每筆都要刷臉或指紋核准，合作夥伴是美國運通、Mastercard、Visa，先開放美國 Pro 用戶，OpenAI 目前不抽成。

這篇文章 OpenAI 推 ChatGPT Wallet：AI 代理替你付款，不碰卡號 最早出現於 鏈新聞 ABMedia 。

OpenAI 11 月 13 日 推出 ChatGPT Wallet ，讓 ChatGPT 的 AI 代理「dots」替用戶付款買東西。OpenAI 說，這是第一個讓代理在拿不到用戶真實卡號的情況下付款，而且每筆消費都要經過安全驗證的錢包，合作夥伴是美國運通、Mastercard 與 Visa。

ChatGPT Wallet 先開放給美國 18 歲以上、使用美國發行合格卡片的 ChatGPT Pro 訂閱用戶。OpenAI 表示，ChatGPT 每週有 12 億人使用，很多人用它研究商品、比較選項、決定要買什麼，現在要幫用戶完成購買。

每筆消費都要刷臉或指紋，代理只拿到單次交易代碼

依 OpenAI 說明，用戶只要綁一次卡，之後每次購買前，會先看到商品、總金額與要扣款的卡片，再用 Face ID 或指紋等安全驗證核准。每次核准都會留下用戶授權代理購買的紀錄。

用戶核准後，支付網路會產生一組付款代碼（token）取代真實卡號，裡面有卡號、安全碼與到期日，只限這筆交易使用。消費照常扣在用戶選的卡上，ChatGPT Wallet 不會把真實卡號交給商家或代理。

OpenAI 說，用戶可以保留原本信用卡的回饋，商品有瑕疵等符合條件的爭議也一樣有保障；用戶直接跟商家交易，定價、出貨、退貨與客服仍由商家負責。OpenAI 也預告，之後用戶可以設定消費上限、購買類別或期間，讓代理在範圍內自動下單。

OpenAI 目前不抽成，先跟商家與發卡機構建立關係

依 CNBC 報導 ，OpenAI 一開始不從交易中抽成，先爭取商家與支付網路合作。負責 OpenAI 營收與支付產品的 Chaya Nayak 對 CNBC 表示，目標是先和商家、支付網路「打下安全又好用的基礎」。

CNBC 指出，OpenAI 去年秋天推出的「Instant Checkout」很快就轉向，今年 3 月改推新版購物功能，ChatGPT Wallet 是在這些嘗試之後再往前一步。美國運通創新主管 Luke Gebb 則說，先限量開放是刻意的，「先在受控的環境開始，再逐步擴大」。

商家端：有網站會擋代理，OpenAI 同步推出合作指南

OpenAI 承認，代理購物還在初期，有些網站可能會不小心擋掉 ChatGPT Wallet 或其他代理付款產品，風控系統也可能把代理下的單當成可疑交易拒絕。CNBC 報導，聯合航空本週表示會封鎖代理訂票，亞馬遜也不讓代理在平台上購物。

OpenAI 同步發布商家合作指南，建議商家在 ChatGPT 認領商家資料、上傳商品資訊，設定 CDN 或防火牆辨識經過簽章的代理請求（Web Bot Auth），並和支付與風控業者溝通。OpenAI 說，正與 Forter、Riskified、Sardine、Signifyd 等防詐業者，以及 Adyen、Checkout.com、Stripe 等支付服務商合作，讓這些系統認得代理發出的合法交易。

這篇文章 OpenAI 推 ChatGPT Wallet：AI 代理替你付款，不碰卡號 最早出現於 鏈新聞 ABMedia 。

articles.title: Coinbase CEO 發文公布四大戰略：重押 AI 金融、推美國股票永續合約，預告 Coinbase Pro 回歸
articles.excerpt:
Coinbase 執行長 Brian Armstrong 於 11 月 13 日發文透露，前一日他在接受 CN […]

〈 Coinbase CEO 發文公布四大戰略：重押 AI 金融、推美國股票永續合約，預告 Coinbase Pro 回歸 〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《 動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體 》。

Coinbase 執行長 Brian Armstrong 於 11 月 13 日發文透露，前一日他在接受 CNBC 採訪時因輝達（NVIDIA）執行長黃仁勳辭職的突發新聞而被迫中斷，因此特地在社群平台公開他原定分享的四大核心戰略：AI 驅動的極致資安、2030 年規模上看 5 兆美元的「代理人金融（AiFi）」、美股代幣化，以及將合規股票永續合約引入美國，文末更驚喜預告「Coinbase Pro」即將回歸。 （前情提要：Coinbase 推出兒童繪本「教加密理財」，每本附 50 美元比特幣） （背景補充：Coinbase 拿下 OCC 聯邦信託銀行正式執照！接手機構級託管業務） 全美最大加密貨幣交易所 Coinbase 共同創辦人兼執行長 Brian Armstrong 於 11 月 13 日在社群平台 X 發表長文，揭露公司下一階段的四大核心戰略佈局。Armstrong 幽默表示，他前一天在財經媒體 CNBC 接受連線專訪時，正巧碰上輝達（NVIDIA）創辦人黃仁勳閃辭的震撼消息而導致訪談被迫打斷，不過他並未在意，隨即將原本準備在節目中暢談的完整商業藍圖搬上社群平台，並拋出「Coinbase Pro 即將推出」的重磅預告。 Got cut off on CBNC yesterday with the Jensen news. All good! Here’s what I was going to talk about: 1) Security. It’s the #1 topic our clients are asking about at the moment, old and new. Trust and security is more important than ever. We’ve always been obsessed with it at… — Brian Armstrong (@brian_armstrong) November 13, 2026 資安防禦導入前沿 AI 模型，99% 資產採冷儲存隔離 在 Armstrong 列出的四大重點中，擺在首位的依然是「安全性（Security）」。他指出，無論是新進還是既有的機構客戶，目前最關切的第一大議題始終是信任與安全。憑藉著對資安的極致要求，目前全球前七大銀行皆選擇與 Coinbase 合作，平台不僅託管著全球規模最龐大的加密資產，更在全球範圍內握有超過 80 張合規牌照。 為了應對日益猖獗的駭客攻擊，Armstrong 透露 Coinbase 正採用最新一代的人工智慧（AI）模型（且往往具備早期搶先存取權）來強化防禦體系，並將超過 99% 的託管資產存放於冷錢包中。在風控哲學上，團隊始終假設「人類一定會受騙」，因此在系統架構上確保沒有任何單一個人、單台筆記型電腦或單一系統能夠獨立轉移客戶資金，並由世界級密碼學家、威脅情報小組及實體安全部隊全天候守備。 重押「代理人金融（AiFi）」：2030 年交易規模上看 5 兆美元 第二大戰略焦點直指人工智慧與加密貨幣的交匯點——「AI 代理人（Agents）」。Armstrong 預測，未來經濟體中的 AI 代理人數量很快就會超越人類，並引發金融格局的劇烈變革；市場預估到 2030 年，由 AI 代理人自主處理的交易規模將高達 3 至 5 兆美元。 他強調，加密貨幣無疑是 AI 代理人最理想的支付與執行軌道，因此 Coinbase 已將打造「最 AI 化的金融帳戶」列為公司最高優先級任務之一，並直言自己對「代理人金融（Agentic Finance，簡稱 AiFi）」的爆發潛力極度看好。 美股代幣化與合規股票永續合約：感謝 SEC 與 CFTC 放下成見 在傳統金融資產上鏈方面，Armstrong 點出了「代幣化（Tokenization）」與「美國境內股票永續合約（Equity Perps）」兩大關鍵賽道： 美股代幣化浪潮：Armstrong 認為，每一位上市公司的執行長都應該希望自家股票實現代幣化。雖然目前仍處於早期階段，但成長動能已不容忽視——目前僅在 Coinbase 旗下 Layer 2 網路 Base 上，代幣化資產的交易量就已突破 50 億美元。相比傳統股票，代幣化股票不僅更易於取得，在與去中心化金融（DeFi）協議組合後更具實用性，例如讓投資人在持有股票的同時額外賺取鏈上收益。 股票永續合約落地美國：Coinbase 多年來持續致力於以負責任且受監管的方式，將熱門的股票永續合約引入美國市場。Armstrong 特別感謝美國證券交易委員會（SEC）主席 Atkins 與美國商品期貨交易委員會（CFTC）主席 Selig 願意放下兩大機構歷史上的管轄權之爭，攜手將這項產品帶給美國投資人。他直言，傳統既得利益者試圖阻擋競爭是徒勞無功的，因為這些產品早已在海外市場蓬勃發展，真正的問題在於美國最終會贏還是會輸，而 Coinbase 決心幫助美國贏得這場競爭。 在貼文的最後，Armstrong 留下了一個令交易員振奮的彩蛋，正式預告「Coinbase Pro 即將推出（coming soon）」，並宣示美國市場的交易體驗即將迎來全面升級。從機構級 AI 資安、AiFi 基礎設施到合規美股衍生品，Coinbase 正試圖將加密貨幣的交易邊界全面推向主流金融的核心腹地。 相關報導 女股神逢低加倉，Ark 買入 660 萬鎂 Coinbase、Circle 與 Robinhood 股票 摩根士丹利降評 Coinbase！目標價砍 53% 至 120 美元、看衰復甦 Coinbase 暗藏比特幣沒下文？Onramp 執行長揭比特幣託管治理的 3 大盲點 助企業自由發行穩定幣支付卡，Coinbase 管錢、Marqeta 管卡〈Coinbase CEO 發文公布四大戰略：重押 AI 金融、推美國股票永續合約，預告 Coinbase Pro 回歸〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。

articles.title: Ethereum Price Predictions: What’s Next for ETH After $2K Fell?
articles.excerpt:
Ethereum has fallen below $2K and entered a major daily demand zone near $1.90K–$1.98K. While this area could support a relief bounce, the persistent bearish structure and nearby liquidation concentrations leave further downside risk in focus. Ethereum Price Analysis: The Daily Chart The daily chart shows Ethereum extending its decline after breaking below the ascending […]

Ethereum has fallen below $2K and entered a major daily demand zone near $1.90K–$1.98K. While this area could support a relief bounce, the persistent bearish structure and nearby liquidation concentrations leave further downside risk in focus.

Ethereum Price Analysis: The Daily Chart

The daily chart shows Ethereum extending its decline after breaking below the ascending channel and failing to sustain subsequent recoveries. The latest selloff has carried the price toward $1.94K, with an intraday wick briefly reaching beneath $1.90K.

ETH is now testing the $1.90K–$1.98K demand zone, which overlaps the consolidation preceding August’s strong advance. This provides a meaningful location for buyers to respond, but the current daily candle remains open, and there is no confirmed reversal yet.

Price also trades below both displayed moving averages, currently around $2.15K and $2.38K. Although their earlier bullish crossover remains visible, the subsequent price breakdown shows that it has not translated into sustained upside momentum. These averages now represent potential recovery hurdles.

A sustained daily close beneath $1.90K would weaken the demand zone and expose the August consolidation lows around $1.83K–$1.87K. The deeper marked support lies near $1.52K–$1.57K. Alternatively, defending demand and reclaiming $2K could initiate a recovery, with the $2.20K–$2.29K supply zone remaining a substantial overhead barrier.

 

ETH/USDT 4-Hour Chart

The four-hour chart highlights an acceleration in selling after Ethereum broke beneath its descending channel’s lower boundary. A subsequent rebound toward the $2.04K–$2.10K zone failed, reinforcing that area as near-term supply before another bearish expansion pushed ETH below $2K.

The latest candles show a modest reaction from approximately $1.90K, but buyers have yet to interrupt the sequence of lower highs and lower lows. A recovery through $1.98K–$2K would be the first sign of stabilization, while reclaiming $2.04K–$2.10K would provide stronger evidence that immediate selling pressure is easing.

Until those levels are recovered, any bounce remains vulnerable to another rejection. Renewed acceptance beneath $1.90K would favor continuation toward the lower daily support references. Conversely, holding demand and forming a higher low would improve the prospects of a broader recovery toward the former consolidation at $2.20K–$2.29K.

 

Sentiment Analysis

The Binance liquidation heatmap shows a prominent concentration of estimated liquidation exposure beneath the current price, around $1.80K–$1.86K. This stands out as a relevant downside area if Ethereum fails to hold the daily demand zone.

A move into this concentration could trigger additional long liquidations and amplify volatility. However, the bright band represents potential forced closures rather than confirmed buying support, so reaching it would not necessarily establish a bottom.

Above the market, liquidation concentrations remain around $1.94K–$1.98K and farther overhead near $2.10K–$2.20K. A sustained recovery through $2K could bring the higher bands into focus and potentially accelerate a rebound through short liquidations.

For now, the bearish structure keeps attention on whether buyers can defend $1.90K. A convincing reclaim of $2K would ease immediate pressure, while another support failure would increase the relevance of the concentrated exposure around $1.80K–$1.86K.

articles.excerpt:
IT之家 11 月 13 日消息，索尼 PlayStation 今天（13 日）晚间宣布，PS5 超分技术 QSSR 即将登陆 《漫威蜘蛛侠 2》《控制：共振》《THE FINALS》《ARC Raiders》 等作品，相关游戏更新将在未来几周内陆续推出。

 

今年 10 月，索尼正式推出了 Quick Spectral Super Resolution（QSSR）技术，为 PS5 带来了 AI 驱动的画面超分辨率升级。

据IT之家了解，该技术和索尼 PlayStation 5 Pro 上使用的 PSSR 类似，可以提升输出画面的清晰度。

QSSR 基于 PS5 Pro 所采用的 PSSR 光谱超分辨率技术的 相同底层架构 开发。与传统超分辨率技术相比，QSSR 能够呈现 更加清晰的细节、更干净的物体边缘 ，以及 更加稳定的画面表现 。

根据介绍，由于 QSSR 与 PSSR 采用相同的接口，因此对于已经支持 PSSR 的游戏而言，接入 QSSR 也更加自然。

此前，索尼互动娱乐（SIE）图形研发首席工程师 Daniel Craig 指出，只需少量调整，旧游戏就能适配 QSSR。

articles.title: Turning Digital Banking Into a Lending Opportunity
articles.excerpt:
Despite the fact that consumers do most of their banking on their phones these days, one core banking function remains largely underutilized in the digital channel: lending. Many banks have yet to fully explore the possibilities of embedded lending, including transaction-based refinancing prompts, goal-based loan assistance, and installment options for card purchases. A report from […]

The post Turning Digital Banking Into a Lending Opportunity appeared first on PaymentsJournal .

Despite the fact that consumers do most of their banking on their phones these days, one core banking function remains largely underutilized in the digital channel: lending. Many banks have yet to fully explore the possibilities of embedded lending, including transaction-based refinancing prompts, goal-based loan assistance, and installment options for card purchases.

A report from Javelin Strategy & Research, Internal Embedded Lending: The Digital Opportunity FIs have in Their Own Backyard , explores why banks have been slow to embrace this opportunity. The key is delivering the right messaging and relevant guidance, making lending offers available at the right time and in the right context without compromising customer trust.

Breaking Down the Silos

Banks have several opportunities to embed lending into their digital channels, including the transaction ledger, bill pay, and personal financial management tool, where customers set and track their financial goals. These are highly visible touchpoints that also give banks access to valuable customer data.

Yet one reason banks have not fully capitalized on these opportunities is that data remains siloed, as do the departments responsible for managing it. As a result, there is often little coordination across different areas of the institution.

“The digital banking folks would very much like to find new opportunities there, as well as the lending folks,” said Dyla n Lerner , Senior Analyst of Digital Banking at Javelin and a co-author of the report. “But how do you bring those two folks together to bring lending opportunities into authenticated digital channels? The financial institutions themselves are not putting these integral pieces together.”

Banks aren’t necessarily using the wealth of information at their disposal to identify the right moments to present lending offers. Yet there are clear points in the customer purchasing journey when such offers could be relevant. Buy now, pay later (BNPL) providers, for example, have become adept at presenting financing options at the point of sale, prompting banks to consider how they might offer similar conveniences within their channels.

“You can be much further in the customer decision purchasing journey,” said Lerner. “A lot of consumers log into their mobile banking app and look at their balance—maybe that’s the right opportunity. Maybe the way you can disintermediate those players at point of sale is by being there earlier.”

However, banks must be careful not to undermine customer trust, especially within their authenticated digital environments. An overly aggressive lending offer could catch customers off guard, particularly when they’re simply exploring their options. Approaching a customer with a loan offer at the wrong moment could feel intrusive, raising privacy concerns and ultimately damaging the relationship.

“We’ve known for a long time that generally consumers have high trust in financial institutions,” said Lerner. “But we also know that trust rides on foot and leaves on horseback.”

Figuring Out Who Is Ready

Lending is highly regulated activity, even when offers are made within a bank’s own digital channels. Bank must be mindful of how they use customer data and avoid targeting individuals in ways that could be considered predatory. So how can they identify when a customer might actually be receptive to a lending offer?

“You look at the customer’s daily balances and you see where are they falling short when it comes to paying bills,” said Disha Bheda , Digital Banking Analyst at Javelin and co-author of the report. “Are they using their overdraft facility? Are they overdue on their credit card bills? And then we try to connect all this data to their life events. Have they recently had a new addition to their family? Does the transaction history point to any life events as such?”

“You monitor all the signals and you monitor the digital behaviors,” she said. “For instance, are they looking at the loan section of the website? These are some of the signals which banks can take into account.”

One possibility is offering customers the option to break a sizable bill or purchase into smaller payments. But making that option appealing requires a seamless experience. Customers shouldn’t have to leave their authenticated banking environment or re-enter information the bank already has on file. Asking them to provide duplicate information creates unnecessary friction. Instead, banks should leverage existing customer data and limit the application process to information that is genuinely new.

Expectations for frictionless payments are higher than ever. Consumers are increasingly accustomed to being offered the option to split purchases into four installments over several weeks, often with little or no additional costs. Banks need to deliver a similarly convenient experience if they hope to compete.

“If I wanted to go to my bank as a source for lending, unless I see a banner ad at the time that just happens to know what I’m looking for, I have to probably go to the public site or to the product page, figure out what the right loan is for me, go to the dropdown of lending services,” said Lerner. “That in and of itself is friction.”

Finding the Opportunities

Every transaction a customer makes through online or mobile banking generates valuable data. Used thoughtfully, that information can help banks identify opportunities to offer relevant lending products while addressing customers’ financial needs.

“It’s an opportunity for FIs to say we know you as a customer and we’re a serious financial institution,” Lerner said. “We are a trusted source of borrowing. We’re here to help you make those decisions and facilitate your financial life. And to me, debt and loans, they’re just as natural a part of financial life as any other banking product or service.”

Many consumers still view their primary financial institution as a place to hold deposits. But banks have the opportunity to play a much more active role.

“We’re a source of lending, and we’re going to remind you of that when you log in at the right place, at the right time, with the right message,” said Lerner. “This is to position the financial institution as a trusted lender, as a source for borrowing. It’s not about throwing lenders at the customer at every possible moment. It’s about how to make this a part of the digital experience.”

The post Turning Digital Banking Into a Lending Opportunity appeared first on PaymentsJournal .

articles.title: 巨乳竟然是罪過？成人RPG《悲觀巨乳混血精靈想要受盡吹捧》Steam商店頁公開
articles.excerpt:
由日本同人社團 PAON 開發的成人探索 RPG《悲觀巨乳混血精靈想要受盡吹捧》Steam 商店頁正式公開！本作以自我肯定感為核心，描述一名因身材遭到排斥的混血精靈，為了尋找認同而踏上旅程的故事。遊戲收錄 70 個以上 H 事件、20 張基本 CG 與超過 400 張差分，預計遊玩時間約 1～2 小時。

 

 

在貧乳至上的精靈村，巨乳竟然成了原罪！？

　　女主角「露米莉亞」擁有精靈與米諾陶洛斯的混血血統，天生擁有豐滿身材，偏偏她居住的精靈村莊奉行「純血與貧乳至上主義」，讓她從小備受排斥。長期缺乏自信的露米莉亞逐漸成為家裡蹲，每天沉迷於自己的興趣，直到某天母親終於忍無可忍，塞給她一點旅費與一根按摩棒，直接將她趕出家門。

 

 

 

 

　　被迫離開故鄉的露米莉亞來到人類城鎮，卻意外發現這裡的審美觀完全不同。過去遭人嫌棄的身材，如今竟成了眾人關注的焦點！究竟這位自我肯定感為零、滿腦子負面想法的混血精靈，能否實現受盡吹捧的幸福生活？

 

 

打工賺錢、提升自我肯定感，越受歡迎就能解鎖越多事件！

　　《悲觀巨乳混血精靈想要受盡吹捧》採用城鎮探索玩法，玩家需要協助露米莉亞透過各種打工與角色互動賺取金錢，同時提升她的「自我肯定感」。從酒館服務生、賭場舞者到其他特殊工作，隨著自我肯定感提高，露米莉亞將逐步解鎖新的場所與成人事件，朝著經濟獨立與自我認同的目標前進。遊戲也準備了大量服裝，包含日常服、兔女郎裝、乳牛比基尼與女服務員裝等，部分事件還會根據服裝產生不同反應。

 

 

 

 

 

 

超過 70 個 H 事件！悲觀精靈的認同感探索之旅

　　本作收錄 20 張基本 CG、400 張以上差分，以及超過 70 個 H 事件，涵蓋打工、換裝、角色互動與各式特殊情境。露米莉亞雖然總是悲觀又缺乏自信，卻十分渴望得到他人的讚美。隨著她在人類城鎮逐漸受到歡迎，角色的心境與行為也會出現變化。遊戲預計遊玩時間約 1～2 小時，並提供回想功能，玩家也能直接開放全部事件，依照自己的喜好欣賞內容。

 

 

 

 

 

 

Steam 商店頁正式公開，歡迎加入願望清單！

　　《悲觀巨乳混血精靈想要受盡吹捧》Steam 商店頁現已正式公開！喜歡巨乳精靈、角色換裝與探索型成人 RPG 的玩家，歡迎前往 Steam 商店頁面將遊戲加入願望清單，掌握後續發售消息！

articles.title: 微软 XBOX 25 周年，CEO 夏尔马称个人将能掌握过去需“举国之力”获得的能力
articles.excerpt:
IT之家 11 月 13 日消息，当地时间 12 日下午，微软 XBOX 负责人阿莎 · 夏尔马发布了一份备忘录， 暗示未来可能利用生成式 AI 辅助游戏开发 。

 

备忘录的标题为《XBOX 的 25 年》，回顾了微软从创立初期的小规模企业发展为拥有数千名员工的公司的历程。不过，真正值得关注的是夏尔马在结尾对未来的展望。

IT之家从备忘录内容获悉，谈及 XBOX 未来 25 年的发展时，夏尔马感叹， 太多游戏创意未能付诸实现 ，即使最终做成游戏，也有不少作品没能达到创作者的预期。“几十年来，想要实现宏大的目标，就只能接受这样的取舍。我们必须改变这种局面。”

“纵观人类历史，创作规模始终受制于能够调动的人力、资金和资源。但这种限制开始被打破了。 过去需要举国之力才能实现的事情，很快一个人就能做到 。今天需要数百名开发者、耗资数亿美元打造的游戏世界，未来一个小团队就能完成。至于我们最大的工作室，也将有能力实现远超当今游戏的宏伟构想，就像《微软模拟飞行 2024》相较于 1982 年的系列初代作品，取得了跨越式的进步。”

外媒 Eurogamer 认为，夏尔马所说的个人将拥有过去需要举国之力才能实现的能力，很容易让人联想到生成式 AI。在接掌 XBOX 之前，夏尔马在微软此前也主要从事 AI 业务。

不过，自担任 CEO 后，夏尔马对生成式 AI 始终保持谨慎态度。当时，她曾明确称自己“无法容忍劣质 AI”。此后几个月，Xbox 又经历了包括大规模重组在内的诸多变化，生成式 AI 也逐渐不再是讨论焦点。

报道指出，这封备忘录暗示着夏尔马此前的 AI 计划开始初露端倪。

articles.title: CHARGESPOT攜手《Pokémon GO》展開全球合作，行動電源借電站化身「補給站」及「道館」助玩家告別電量焦慮
articles.excerpt:
行動電源共享服務品牌 CHARGESPOT 營運商 INFORICH 株式會社（以下簡稱 INFORICH）宣布與由 Scopely Explore Inc. 及 The Pokémon Company 共同營運的手機定位遊戲《Pokémon GO》展開全新合作。將 CHARGESPOT 借電站導入《Pokémon GO》遊戲地圖，串聯玩家的遊戲體驗與實體場域。自 2026 年 11 月 14 日起，日本、香港、台灣、泰國、新加坡、英國、義大利、澳洲及美國等 9 個國家及地區，約 3 萬個 CHARGESPOT 借電站將陸續成為遊戲內的「寶可補給站」與「道館」，讓玩家在探索遊戲世界的同時，也能就近租借行動電源。

 

 

　　INFORICH 秉持「Bridging Beyond Borders」的使命，以「場景 × 科技」（Location × Technology）為核心理念。透過結合實體據點與數位應用，CHARGESPOT 不僅提供行動電源共享服務，也進一步串聯玩家的遊戲體驗與真實城市空間，讓原本日常經過的地點成為探索城市的新起點。

 

 

　　《Pokémon GO》以 GPS 定位結合實地探索，吸引全球玩家走進城市每個角落。遊戲自 2016 年 7 月推出以來，每年均躋身全球十大手機遊戲之列，將整個世界變成玩家的遊樂場。此次合作中，設於購物中心、交通樞紐及旅遊景點等日常生活場所的 CHARGESPOT 租借據點，將化身為遊戲內的「寶可補給站」及「道館」。當玩家收集道具、參與道館對戰及團體戰時，這些地點亦將成為國內外訓練家發掘和到訪的全新據點。

　　此外，玩家在收集道具或參與團體戰期間，可現場租借行動電源。透過探索熟悉的遊戲介面與便捷的現場充電服務，INFORICH 期望讓玩家無需擔心電量耗盡，盡情探索城市、暢玩遊戲。

 

關於 CHARGESPOT

　　CHARGESPOT 是全球首家提供行動電源跨國租賃服務的品牌，2017 年服務起始於香港，其母公司為日本 INFORICH。目前穩定在台灣、日本、港澳、泰國、新加坡、澳洲、義大利、英國、美國等地提供服務。CHARGESPOT 共享行動電源服務不僅提供甲借乙還，在有提供服務的國家都能跨國租還。

articles.title: 《燕雲十六聲》V2.4「滹沱」帶來週年重磅版本史詩大戰開打，歡慶週年零門檻登入送「千元自選時裝」
articles.excerpt:
由網易遊戲旗下 Everstone Studio 打造、龍邑遊戲代理的武俠開放世界動作冒險 RPG《燕雲十六聲》，即將於 11 月 13 日開啟週年慶版本「滹沱」。正逢《燕雲十六聲》一週年之際，江湖將以一場盛大慶典，邀請玩家參與遊戲迄今最宏大、最扣人心弦的敘事篇章，並帶來上線以來最豐厚的福利——總價值高達 5,000 台幣的福利大放送。與此同時，「滹沱」也帶來多部劇情內容、雙槍武學、鎮守、野外首領及兩種全新棋局玩法；更多週年活動獎勵也將陸續登場，為新老玩家帶來豐富的週年回饋。

 

 

抵達「滹沱」，回望一場跨越十六年的戰爭

　　在不見山前兩片區域中，玩家已逐步走近墨山道，了解這個隱世群體的當下處境與過往傳承。而「滹沱」作為不見山的最後一塊擴展區域，將故事的視角從深山中的機關、秘聞與桃源，進一步帶向山外的河流、城鎮與戰場。「滹沱」地處南北交界，是一片飽經戰火的土地。隨著契丹南下、舊日盟約破裂，滹沱河再次成為戰爭的中心。大量百姓被迫南遷，與此同時，來自各地的江湖義士也紛紛奔赴前線集結，兩大政權的主力即將在此展開一場史詩般的決戰。

 

　　對於少東家與江叔而言，「滹沱」還承載著一段未曾揭開的往事。這片戰場與十六年前的戰爭緊密相連，隨著玩家重返「滹沱」，一些被戰火掩埋多年的秘密也將逐漸浮出水面。此外，玩家還可體驗俠跡「奉敕不殺」、「蘆中曲」、「螢燭照夜」等全新劇情內容，從不同人物的視角，呈現戰爭之下的江湖百態。

 

　　而「俠」的答案，也將在這些故事中被重新追問：當忠義陷入兩難，究竟該為搖搖欲墜的皇權而戰，還是為了守護故土與無辜百姓挺身而出？在「滹沱」，「俠」並非對權勢與舊約的盲目追隨，而是在時代洪流中，仍願意為心中的正義作出選擇。

 

 

更強勁的對戰，全新鎮守與野外首領加入戰局

　　週年慶版本還將帶來全新的戰鬥挑戰。全新鎮守「滹沱河」將帶領玩家踏入戰火籠罩的前線，直面擁有「血訣霸體」的契丹猛將蕭翰，迎接更具挑戰性的戰鬥。隨著「滹沱」故事持續推進，野外首領天涯客「丙申」與「耶律阿不里」也將登場。前者背負未能趕赴滹沱河畔的遺憾，獨守藏月崗；後者則以契丹王族與薩滿的身份，為一場獻祭踏入戰火之地。玩家將在開放世界中挑戰他們，並追尋這些人物與「滹沱」往事之間的聯繫。

 

 

袁和平指導雙槍武學，帶來全新戰鬥節奏

　　全新的雙槍武學將於 11 月 26 日正式上線。《燕雲十六聲》特別邀請國際知名動作指導袁和平導演參與動捕設計。袁和平導演曾指導《臥虎藏龍》等知名電影，並擔任《燕雲十六聲》全球動作顧問。

 

　　雙槍流派【鳴金 · 霆】由輕槍與重槍兩套槍法構成：輕槍承擔主要輸出，重槍側重架勢反擊。兩套槍法圍繞「槍勢」的積累與強化展開，透過易武技串聯攻勢，輕重交替銜接，形成招招相承的連招循環。此外，由袁和平指導設計的另一款全新武器「盤龍棍」，也將在後續版本中與玩家見面。

 

兩大全新棋局玩法上線，策略與趣味兼備

　　除開放世界探索與戰鬥內容外，週年慶版本還將帶來兩種全新棋局玩法，為玩家提供更加多元的休閒與策略體驗。在「打馬棋」中，玩家將親自化身棋子，透過擲骰決定前進步數，並以率先抵達終點為目標展開競爭。棋盤中融入了遊戲中的奇術、武學與經典場景，讓玩家在輕鬆的對局中，重溫江湖旅途裡的熟悉記憶。

 

　　另一種全新策略玩法「江湖弈」，則將《燕雲十六聲》中的俠影、武學與江湖關係帶上棋盤。玩家可圍繞不同俠影與戰鬥定位組建陣容，並透過佈陣、裝備分配、招式搭配與回合運營，尋找適合自己的制勝策略。

 

歡慶週年零門檻登入送「千元自選時裝」豪灑5000台幣福利

　　過去一年，《燕雲十六聲》從清河出發，陸續探索開封、河西等風格各異的區域，並持續透過版本更新拓展武俠世界的邊界。從 PC 端、PlayStation 5 到手機端與 Xbox，越來越多玩家在這片江湖中相遇。

　　歡慶一週年，11 月 13 日週年慶版本「滹沱」將帶來超過價值 5,000 台幣的福利，等待玩家登入領取：

 

零門檻登錄送：價值 2580 長鳴珠外觀 12 選 1

上線輕鬆領：裊裊之音 *42 ​+​ 繞梁之音 *27

11月~12月更多好禮：5 套免費服裝與海量配飾道具

articles.title: 《三國群英傳：策定九州》全新逐鹿賽季「群英並起」消息釋出，回歸混戰地圖與新武將前瞻
articles.excerpt:
由宇峻奧汀發行的跨平台三國策略遊戲《三國群英傳：策定九州》，今（13）日公開全新逐鹿賽季「群英並起」沙盤地圖與勢力特性系統，宣布回歸經典自由混戰模式，並同步釋出傳說武將「孫策」與「大喬」解析。此外，官方亦宣布「亞洲服」伺服器持續火熱加開，人氣盟主「熊班長」NL 正式進駐創盟，活動祭出總值百萬好禮與「大摩 15 年三國群英傳專屬紀念酒」，號召各路主公搶先集結；同時預告台港澳與東南亞首場跨區匹配伺服器 12/5 登場，在逐鹿賽季「漢魏爭鋒」正面交鋒。

 

 

全新沙盤地圖公開
勢力混戰、特性系統助陣問鼎

　　新賽季「群英並起」回歸自由混戰模式。各盟將自關中、中州、江漢三座二級資源州挺進司隸，角逐二級州 6 級與 9 級城、司隸 11 級城及中心 13 級城池，共計 270 個問鼎名額。賽季結算時依佔領城池直接發放獎勵，問鼎同盟更可額外獲得專屬「聯盟問鼎裝扮」。同步登場的「勢力特性」系統於選州後立即解鎖基礎特性，主公可透過分配特性點獲取戰力加成，系統涵蓋基礎、普通、羈絆、高級至終極五大檔次，為瞬息萬變的戰局增添更多策略深度。

 

 

江東小霸王「孫策」登場
集減傷、反彈與不滅於一體的前排鐵壁

　　勇冠三軍、奠定江東基業的傳說武將「孫策」即將於新賽季登場。作為以「固守反彈」與「不滅機制」為核心的頂級前排防禦武將，孫策不僅能在承受大量傷害的同時反彈部分傷害，遭多支部隊集火時更能觸發「不滅」狀態；若搭配普攻追擊體系，還能持續堆疊防禦與反彈效果，成為敵軍難以突破的戰場鐵壁。

 

 

絕代佳人「大喬」傾城亮相
集牽引、追擊增益與普攻輸出於一體的戰術核心

　　絕代風華、氣韻溫婉的江東佳人「大喬」翩然登場。大喬定位為以「牽引」與「追擊增益」為核心的戰術型輔助，當編制為近戰部隊時，能強制敵方攻擊自身，同時大幅拉升團隊的追擊機率與普攻傷害，是江東盾體系中完美銜接控制與輸出的關鍵樞紐。

 

 

傳說武將「馬超」、「關羽」全新外觀霸氣登場

　　官方同步推出傳說武將「馬超」與「關羽」全新外觀，並附帶專屬限定動態頭像框與個人介面裝飾，助主公於戰場上盡展無雙風範，彰顯萬夫莫敵的豪傑氣概。

 

 

首場跨區匹配 12/5 登場
台港澳與東南亞開打「漢魏爭鋒」

　　伺服器 S2-012～013 將於 12/05 與東南亞服 S2-008～010 匹配，共同進入逐鹿賽季「漢魏爭鋒」。跨地域對決考驗不同語言環境下的外交博弈與聯盟默契，讓爭奪中原之爭更具挑戰性。官方表示，後續將陸續推出更多跨區域對決，以及更多區域加入亞洲服行列。

 

　　亞洲服伺服器持續加開，「熊班長」NL 也已進駐創盟，誓與主公共奪首屆問鼎榮耀！凡於活動期間進駐亞洲服伺服器，完成預約即領聚義令 ×10；加入已完成預創盟的聯盟，全盟最高可領聚義令 ×2,415；賽季結算第一名再加碼聚義令 ×50，盟主另獲「大摩 15 年策定九州專屬紀念酒」。更多資訊懇請持續關注官方粉絲團。

articles.title: 比特幣財庫公司 Nakamoto 欠款 1.65 億美元，比市值還高
articles.excerpt:
Nakamoto 向 Kraken 借 1.65 億枚 USDT，超過約 1.04 億美元市值，已把 12 月到期的 6,000 萬延到 2027 年；以太坊財庫公司 BTCS 也認賠賣幣保住 Aave 借款。

這篇文章 比特幣財庫公司 Nakamoto 欠款 1.65 億美元，比市值還高 最早出現於 鏈新聞 ABMedia 。

比特幣跌破 7 萬美元後，拿比特幣當抵押借錢的財庫公司壓力浮上檯面。由 David Bailey 創辦的比特幣財庫公司 Nakamoto（NAKA）向 Kraken 借了 1.65 億枚 USDT，依 CoinDesk 報導 ，Nakamoto 股價 12 日收在 5.79 美元，市值約 1.04 億美元，欠款已經比整家公司的市值還高。

Nakamoto 12 日提交的 8-K 申報 顯示，公司 11 月 11 日和 Kraken 簽訂借款合約第二次修正，把原本 12 月 4 日到期的 6,000 萬枚 USDT 延到 2027 年 12 月 4 日；其餘 1.05 億枚 USDT 仍在 2027 年 6 月 30 日到期，今年已經沒有要還的部分。

4,283 枚比特幣有 3,030 枚押在 Kraken

依 Nakamoto 的 第三季季報 ，截至 9 月 30 日，公司持有 4,283 枚比特幣，成本 5.06 億美元、公允價值 3.58 億美元，其中 3,030 枚質押給貸款方。依表計算，平均買進成本約 11.8 萬美元。

CoinDesk 計算，以比特幣跌破 6.9 萬美元的價格，這 3,030 枚約值 2.08 億美元，約是欠款的 126%。如果抵押品價值跌破維持水位，Nakamoto 就得還掉部分借款、追加比特幣，或兩者都做；公司還有約 1,253 枚沒有質押的比特幣可以補，約值 8,600 萬美元。

這次修約也讓 Kraken 把 Nakamoto 在 Kraken 的衍生品部位淨值，計入抵押品價值，由 Kraken 每天計算，淨值為負時以零計。CoinDesk 指出，Nakamoto 9 月底買了 2,000 枚比特幣、履約價 5.5 萬美元的賣權，但這批賣權 12 月 25 日到期，早於借款到期日。Nakamoto 投資長 Tyler Evans 說：「這次修約延長了我們的跑道，也讓抵押品部位更有韌性。」

以太坊財庫公司 BTCS 認賠賣幣，保住 Aave 借款

以以太幣為主要資產的那斯達克上市公司 BTCS 也面臨類似壓力。BTCS 12 日提交的 季報 寫道：「出售以太幣的價格低於原始成本，是公司主動管理抵押水位與 DeFi 借款健康係數的一部分。」

季報顯示，截至 11 月 9 日，BTCS 在借貸協議 Aave 上的借款約 6,410 萬美元（含應計利息），以約 46,676 枚以太幣擔保，以當天每枚 2,127 美元計算價值 9,930 萬美元。BTCS 9 月底現金只有約 46.3 萬美元。

CoinDesk 依 11 月 9 日的數字估算，以太幣跌到約 1,717 美元時，BTCS 的借款可能開始被清算，比 13 日約 1,950 美元的價格低約 12%；但 BTCS 的部位在 11 月 9 日之後可能已經變動。鏈新聞稍早也整理了 比特幣跌破 6.9 萬美元的爆倉情況 。

這篇文章 比特幣財庫公司 Nakamoto 欠款 1.65 億美元，比市值還高 最早出現於 鏈新聞 ABMedia 。

articles.title: 鴻海怎麼讓人形機器人進工廠？郭柳宗：先拆任務，再決定哪一段需要 AI
articles.excerpt:
人形機器人進工廠，不一定得先學會雙足走路，也不一定每項工作都需要靈巧手。鴻海科技集團機器人事業處總經理郭柳宗在近日舉辦的 333 Robots Community Meetup 分享，目前團隊把不少心力放在 SMT 產線、倉儲等既有製造場景，希望先把特定任務做成熟，再往更多相似場域延伸。對工廠來說，機器人不只是要能完成動作，速度、定位精度、力控與穩定性，也都會影響它能不能真正進入產線。 從陪伴機器人做到工廠，面對的是另一種任務 郭柳宗也是女媧創造（NUWA Robotics）創辦人。十年前創業時，他最初想做的是陪伴型機器人。因為曾長期在海外工作、女兒成長時自己不常在身邊，他當時曾想像，如果有一台機器人能替遠方的爸爸陪孩子講故事、跳舞、互動，也許能補上部分陪伴。後來女媧的產品也一路延伸到教育與企業應用。 如今到了鴻海，他面對的則是另一種機器人問題。郭柳宗提到，集團本身有大量 SMT 產線與倉儲場景，因此只要一個共通場景能做成熟，就有機會進一步往更多工廠部署。相較之下，工廠對機器人的要求也更具體：除了完成任務，還得考慮動作速度、位置精度，以及組裝時所需的力控能力。 硬體形式也得跟著場景調整。郭柳宗表示，就目前團隊鎖定的工廠應用來看，輪式底盤在速度、穩定性與成本上更容易符合需求，因此現階段會先以輪式平台為主。相較之下，雙足機器人還要處理平衡、耗能，以及更多關節帶來的成本問題。 目前視覺語言動作模型（Vision-Language-Action Model，VLA）已能控制機器人執行抓取，但郭柳宗以團隊測試經驗說明，模型執行動作的速度與誤差仍可能影響工廠使用；部分組裝作業還需要精準控制施力大小，不能只做到「抓得到」。 整段工作還沒全交給 AI，先把任務拆成不同節點 因此，郭柳宗分享，目前團隊會利用行為樹（Behavior Tree）把複雜工作拆成不同節點，再決定哪些部分需要 VLA，而不是把整串流程全部交給端到端模型。 例如，機器人從 A 點移動到料架，可以使用既有控制方式；到了需要從料架辨識並取出指定物件的環節，再交由 VLA 處理。郭柳宗指出，以現階段技術而言，如果整段任務都使用 VLA，執行速度仍是一項瓶頸。 團隊也開發了動作任務編排工具，讓工程師可以用拖拉方式把一個工作拆成不同節點，工具中並內建模擬功能，可以預先模擬機器人的動作。真正需要模型學習的任務，則得進一步蒐集資料、訓練，再部署到實際場景。 郭柳宗在簡報中以一段訓練案例說明，團隊會讓操作人員戴上 VR 裝置，透過控制器操作機器人反覆完成抓取與放置，這類任務可能需要累積數百次示範，才能取得後續訓練所需的資料。除了真實世界的遙控操作（Teleoperation），團隊也會利用模擬環境讓機器人學習動作。 世界動作模型（World Action Model）也是郭柳宗提到的技術之一。他表示，這類模型具備一定的泛化能力，希望降低不同場景都得重新蒐集大量訓練資料的負擔；不同任務訓練出的技能，也可以整理到技能庫，再依部署場域下載所需能力。 工廠資料怎麼變成機器人技能？光有資料還不夠 談到機器人 AI，郭柳宗認為鴻海的一項優勢，在於製造現場擁有大量生產資料。團隊的做法不是從頭訓練大型基礎模型，而是在既有預訓練模型上，利用生產資料進行後訓練（Post-training），讓機器人進一步學會工廠需要的特定技能。 不過，資料也不是蒐集得越多就越好。郭柳宗以「資料健康度」說明，如果原本只想教機器人把物件從左邊拿到右邊，蒐集的影片卻混入把物件拿回原位等不必要動作，或背景帶入太多無關資訊，都可能干擾後續訓練，因此資料進入模型前仍需要檢查與整理。 他也分享，依團隊經驗，VLA 經過模仿學習後，特定任務的成功率可能約八成；再將成功與失敗案例納入強化學習（Reinforcement Learning），可以提高到 95% 以上。但郭柳宗直言，「95% 在工廠也是不行的」，團隊目前希望把成功率進一步做到 99% 以上。 人形機器人的手，為什麼不一定要像人的手？ 硬體選擇也得回到實際工作。郭柳宗表示，目前團隊並非所有任務都使用多指靈巧手，而是會依不同場景設計專用的末端執行器。 他以 SMT 捲料為例，工廠裡的料盤可能彼此緊密堆疊，靈巧手的手指反而太厚，不容易伸進狹窄縫隙。因此團隊針對這項工作設計薄型夾爪，讓夾爪能直接伸入料盤之間，把指定捲料取出。郭柳宗也提到，除了能不能完成動作，成本與投資效益也是選擇末端工具時必須考慮的條件。 從任務拆解、VLA、模擬與世界動作模型，到後訓練和專用夾爪，郭柳宗這次分享提供的是一個很具體的工廠視角：人形機器人要進入產線，不只是把更強的 AI 模型裝上機器人，而是要從實際工作往回決定哪些環節需要 […]
